question.worked_solution:
We will use the fact that the dot product is linear.

To quickly compute the numerator $u\cdot (10v),$ we multiply $u\cdot v$ by $10.$ Doing this, we get

$$
\begin{aligned}u\cdot (10v) & =10(u\cdot v) \\  & =10\cdot (-2) \\  & =-20.\end{aligned}
$$

To quickly compute the denominator $u\cdot (4u),$ we compute $u\cdot u$ first and then multiply the result by $4.$ Doing this, we get

$$
\begin{aligned}u\cdot (4u) & =4(u\cdot u) \\  & =4({u}_{1}^{2}+{u}_{2}^{2}+{u}_{3}^{2}+{u}_{4}^{2}) \\  & =4((-1)^{2}+{2}^{2}+{1}^{2}+(-2)^{2}+(-1)^{2}) \\  & =4(1+4+1+4+1) \\  & =4\cdot 11 \\  & =44.\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore,

$$
\frac{u\cdot (10v)}{u\cdot (4u)}=\frac{-20}{44}=-\frac{5}{11}.
$$
